taxonomy.subtopic: Autonomous aldosterone secretion, renin suppression, and distal nephron ion transport

questions.stem_html: A 49-year-old man has resistant hypertension, muscle weakness, serum potassium of 2.9 mEq/L, and serum bicarbonate of 33 mEq/L. The accompanying panel shows high aldosterone and suppressed renin. Which renal effect best links the hormone abnormality to both electrolyte findings?

options.text_html: Increased epithelial sodium channel activity creates a lumen-negative potential that promotes potassium secretion by principal cells and hydrogen secretion by alpha-intercalated cells
Reduced proximal sodium reabsorption increases potassium retention and bicarbonate loss
Inhibition of the Na⁺-K⁺-2Cl⁻ cotransporter reduces potassium and hydrogen secretion
Reduced distal sodium delivery prevents potassium secretion despite aldosterone excess
Suppression of Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase activity causes intracellular potassium accumulation in principal cells

questions.explanation_html: Autonomous aldosterone increases ENaC and basolateral Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase activity in principal cells. Sodium reabsorption makes the tubular lumen more negative, favoring potassium secretion. Aldosterone also stimulates hydrogen secretion by alpha-intercalated cells. Volume expansion suppresses renin, while potassium and hydrogen losses produce hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Primary hyperaldosteronism enhances distal sodium reabsorption; proximal bicarbonate loss is not the mechanism.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Loop-diuretic action does not explain autonomous aldosterone with suppressed renin.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Aldosterone-driven sodium reabsorption occurs with sufficient distal sodium delivery to promote potassium loss.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Aldosterone increases rather than suppresses Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase activity.

questions.educational_objective: Primary hyperaldosteronism causes sodium retention with renin suppression and increases distal potassium and hydrogen ion secretion, producing hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.
